decisions.question: The self-contained gate (Rule 2: 'Every contract, ADR and OQ id the file names has its text inline in its section. Other phases' ids appear only in the Phase block's Dependencies and Collides with lines') flags ids that occur only inside verbatim excerpts. How does it apply, given S98's and S102's precedent? The set here: contract ids bus-api@v2, flutter-binding@v2, navigation-api@v1, nidana-checks@v1, topic-codegen@v1, topic-model@v1, topology-dsl@v2, topology-ir@v1; OQ ids OQ8, OQ9, OQ12, OQ-T2, OQ-F1; other-phase ids nidana.flutter.1, nidana.model.1 to .5 and .7 outside Dependencies and Collides with. Unlike nidana.model.1 and .2, this phase's own Verification names topic-model@v1 (its binding loads once nidana.model.5 has merged), and its Scope names slugs and guarantee ids (bus-api, topology-dsl/G{n}, bus_activation_test.dart) that are neither consumed nor produced.

decisions.chosen: Apply the gate to ids the file selects; excerpt-internal citations stay as the source's words
decisions.why: Same reasoning as S98 and S102: the Contracts and Open questions selection rules and Rule 1 cannot all hold under a reading of Rule 2 that counts every id inside a mandated excerpt. What differs here is the reference to topic-model@v1 in the phase's Verification line. It is a statement about what the replay of a binding shows once the declarations exist, not an Interface this phase implements: the phase's Scope states the whole behavior it builds (the binding rule, the runner choice by the flutter_test import, the PENDING rule, the restriction by ids read from the conformance library's import path, the anchored name filter and the not-run-counts-as-passing rule), and the fixtures it runs are data under hsdd/contract/fixture/. The synthetic suites its tests bind live in a temporary workspace. So nothing the implementer builds is missing from the file. A skill wording that scoped Rule 2 to selected ids, or told the writer to inline cited contracts, would have changed my mind.
